To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the poor in Chile are experiencing a process of social inclusion that is characterized by the emergence of a new form of welfare citizenship, one that is based on the recognition of the poor in terms of their needs, and not on their rights as citizens.

the expansion of social policies has provided a significant increase in social inclusion of the poor; however, this expansion has been accompanied by a reduction in the recognition of the poor and a deterioration in the terms and conditions in which they experience welfare.

, while the expansion of social programmes in Chile has been a positive step towards the inclusion of the poor, it has not provided the conditions for the poor to experience social recognition and to become active and effective subjects of rights, as they are still treated as passive recipients of charity.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the quality of the citizenship implications of contemporary social assistance policies in Latin America, in particular the extent to which they provide conditions of recognition of the poor and the type of citizenship that is being experienced by current welfare beneficiaries in the region.
the question of whether the poor are experiencing a "new welfare citizenship" as a result of the expansion of social protection policies.
the quality of welfare inclusion of the poorest segments of the population in the country, and its implications in terms of the citizenship status of poor people in the country.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
social assistance policies have been able to provide some conditions of welfare inclusion for poor Chileans, although they are still limited and unequal.

the expansion of social policies and social assistance programmes in the last decade have not been able to reverse the exclusionary effects produced by the neo liberal transformation of welfare in the country and, therefore, the welfare regime that has been established in Chile is still highly exclusionary, with a strong tendency to reproduce and reinforce stratification and social segregation, and with limited capacity to provide conditions of welfare inclusion and social recognition of people living in poverty.

, although the welfare regime established under neo liberal policies in Chile has provided conditions of welfare inclusion to the poor in the country, these are highly stratified in nature, and are not based on the recognition of their status as subjects of rights, but rather, as clients and recipients of welfare services.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expansion of social policies in the country has not only failed to provide conditions of social recognition for the poor, but has also reinforced their status as a marginal group in society.

the findings suggest that the current expansion of social assistance has not only provided the poor with access to a minimum set of social rights, but also with a set of opportunities for the poor to become active citizens.
the expansion of social protection policies in Chile, as well as the welfare citizenship that they produce, are the result of the complex interplay between social and political forces.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, while social assistance policies have been instrumental in providing the poor with access to basic social goods, their impacts in relation to the recognition of the poor are ambiguous, as the poor are still perceived as passive subjects of welfare assistance.

despite the fact that the expansion of social policies under the neo liberal regime has provided a significant increase in welfare coverage, the terms of inclusion of poor people in the Chilean welfare field remain highly stratified and exclusionary, and are characterized by the persistence of social stigma and the reproduction of social inequalities.

the welfare inclusion of poor people in Chile is still limited by their exclusion from the labour market, and that this is a major obstacle to the recognition of the poor and the development of a welfare citizenship.
